elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
On a public highway or street
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, drugs, or a combination
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
notes: Mississippi uses a 5-year lookback for DUI sentencing. Implied consent under § 63-11-5. Administrative license suspension 90 days first offense. Non-adjudication available for first offense.

penalty_max: 48 hours in jail or 48 hours community service
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle on a public road
While under the influence or with BAC .08+
No prior DUI convictions within 5 years
notes: Eligible for non-adjudication (MASEP program). 90-day license suspension. Ignition interlock may be ordered.

penalty_min: 5 days or 10 days community service (second); 1 year (third); 2 years (fourth+)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence or with BAC .08+
One or more prior DUI convictions within 5 years
mandatory_minimum: 5 days or 10 days community service (second); 1 year and 1 day (third); 2 years (fourth+)
enhancements: Fourth or subsequent offense (habitual DUI offender)
notes: Second offense: 2-year suspension. Third: 5-year suspension. Fourth+: lifetime revocation. Lookback period is 5 years.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle on a public road
While under the influence of any substance that impairs driving ability
Including controlled substances, prescription medications, or any drug
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of drugs and alcohol
notes: No per se drug limit. Prosecution relies on impairment evidence and toxicology. Same penalties as alcohol DUI.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle in willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. Points assessed against driving record.

statute_title: Duty to Stop — Accident Involving Death or Injury
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in death, injury, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop and remain at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render aid
notes: Hit-and-run resulting in death is a felony. License revocation upon conviction.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Defendant's operation caused the death of another person
notes: DUI death carries up to 25 years. May also be charged under manslaughter statutes.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through culpably negligent operation of a motor vehicle
notes: Culpable negligence is a higher standard than ordinary negligence. May be charged in addition to or instead of DUI death.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the suspension
notes: Driving on a DUI-suspended license carries enhanced penalties. Additional suspension upon conviction.

statute_title: Fleeing or Eluding a Law Enforcement Officer
elements: A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Signal was by siren, emergency lights, or other lawful means
Defendant willfully failed to stop
Defendant attempted to flee by operating the vehicle recklessly
enhancements: Causing death or serious bodily injury
notes: Officer must be in uniform and operating a marked vehicle, or defendant must otherwise know it is law enforcement.

offense_class: Felony (Schedule I/II); Misdemeanor (Schedule III-V small amounts)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Mississippi Uniform Controlled Substances Law schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription
enhancements: Possession near a school, church, or public park (§ 41-29-142)
notes: Mississippi treats most simple possession as a felony for Schedule I/II substances. Drug court diversion programs available.

statute_title: Possession of Marijuana — 30 Grams or Less
offense_class: Misdemeanor (30g or less first); Felony (over 30g or subsequent)
penalty_max: 90 days (first, 30g or less); 1 year (subsequent, 30g or less); 3 years (over 30g)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Without lawful authority
notes: Mississippi decriminalized small amounts (30g or less) for first offense. Over 30g or subsequent offenses are felonies. Medical marijuana legalized 2022.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance in Mississippi
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or church
notes: Simple possession is a felony. Larger quantities trigger trafficking charges under § 41-29-139(f).

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or church
notes: Meth is a significant enforcement priority in Mississippi. Manufacturing carries separate enhanced penalties.

penalty_min: 10 years (cocaine 200-500g); varies by substance and weight
penalty_max: 30 years (most); Life (large quantities or certain substances)
elements: Defendant knowingly sold, manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A quantity of controlled substance meeting trafficking thresholds
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (most trafficking thresholds, cannot be reduced or suspended)
notes: Trafficking thresholds: cocaine 200g, heroin 200g, methamphetamine 200g. Mandatory minimums cannot be suspended or paroled.

statute_title: Sale, Distribution, or Manufacture of Controlled Substance
penalty_max: 30 years (Schedule I/II); 10 years (Schedule III/IV); 5 years (Schedule V)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally sold, delivered, manufactured, or possessed with intent to sell or deliver
A controlled substance
enhancements: Distribution near a school, church, or park (§ 41-29-142)
notes: Second offense penalties are doubled. Third offense carries life imprisonment for Schedule I/II.

elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured a controlled substance
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a child
notes: Methamphetamine manufacturing (§ 41-29-313) carries additional penalties and cleanup costs.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With knowledge that it would be used to plant, propagate, test, analyze, pack, or consume a controlled substance
enhancements: Sale or delivery of paraphernalia to a minor
notes: Misdemeanor offense. Sale of paraphernalia to a minor carries enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
With intent to sell, deliver, or distribute
enhancements: Near a school, church, or park
notes: Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, and other indicators. Same penalties as actual distribution.

elements: Defendant willfully killed a human being
With deliberate design
Under circumstances enumerated in § 97-3-19(2) (e.g., during robbery, sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, or killing a peace officer)
mandatory_minimum: Life without parole (if death not imposed)
enhancements: Murder of a law enforcement officer
Murder during commission of enumerated felony
notes: Mississippi retains the death penalty. Capital murder requires specific aggravating circumstances. Non-capital murder (§ 97-3-19(1)) carries life imprisonment.

elements: Defendant killed a human being
With deliberate design to effect the death
Without circumstances elevating to capital murder
notes: Mississippi does not formally distinguish first and second-degree murder. Non-capital murder carries 20 years to life.

elements: Defendant killed a human being
Without malice, in the heat of passion
By a cruel or unusual weapon
Or in an unnecessary manner
notes: Mississippi manslaughter statute is broad. Heat of passion is the classic voluntary manslaughter scenario.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through culpable negligence
Without intent to kill
notes: Culpable negligence is higher than ordinary negligence but less than intent. Includes deaths from reckless behavior.

elements: Defendant attempted to cause or purposely, knowingly, or recklessly caused serious bodily injury to another
Or attempted to cause or caused bodily injury with a deadly weapon or other means likely to produce death or serious injury
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Aggravated domestic violence (§ 97-3-7(4)) carries specific enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant attempted to cause or purposely, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
Or negligently caused bodily injury with a deadly weapon
Or attempted by physical menace to put another in fear of imminent serious injury
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Simple assault includes both physical contact and threatening conduct. Low-level misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant caused or attempted to cause bodily injury
With a deadly weapon or other means likely to produce death or serious injury
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Deadly weapon includes any object used in a manner capable of causing death or serious injury.

elements: Defendant feloniously took the personal property of another
From the person or in the presence of the person
Against the person's will by violence or putting in fear
notes: Simple robbery without a weapon. Armed robbery is a separate, more serious offense.

elements: Defendant feloniously took the personal property of another
By putting the person in fear of immediate injury
While exhibiting a deadly weapon
notes: Armed robbery carries a mandatory minimum of 3 years that cannot be suspended. Maximum is life imprisonment.

penalty_max: 30 years (general); Life (if ransom demanded or victim sexually assaulted)
elements: Defendant willfully seized, confined, or kidnapped another person
With intent to secretly confine, hold for ransom, or cause bodily injury
notes: Kidnapping of a child carries enhanced penalties. Separate from unlawful restraint.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously set fire to or burned a dwelling
Or aided, counseled, or procured the burning
notes: First-degree arson involves dwellings. Second-degree (§ 97-17-3) involves non-dwelling structures. Third-degree (§ 97-17-5) involves personal property.

penalty_max: 20 years (attempt at non-capital murder); Life (attempt at capital murder)
elements: Defendant designed and endeavored to kill another person
Defendant took a substantial step toward the killing
enhancements: Victim was a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempted murder carries up to half the maximum of the completed offense for non-capital murder, or up to life for capital murder attempt.

penalty_max: 5 years (grand larceny $1,000–$5,000); 10 years ($5,000–$25,000); 20 years ($25,000+); 6 months (petit larceny)
elements: Defendant took and carried away personal property of another
Without consent
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Mississippi raised the felony theft threshold to $1,000 in 2014. Graduated sentencing based on value.

elements: Defendant took and carried away personal property of another
Value exceeded $1,000
With intent to permanently deprive
notes: Grand larceny threshold is $1,000 in Mississippi.

elements: Defendant took and carried away personal property of another
Value was $1,000 or less
With intent to permanently deprive
notes: Third petit larceny conviction is elevated to a felony carrying up to 5 years.

elements: Defendant willfully concealed or took possession of retail merchandise
Without paying full purchase price
With intent to convert to personal use
notes: Separate shoplifting statute. Third shoplifting conviction regardless of value is a felony.

elements: Defendant broke and entered a building, structure, or dwelling
With intent to commit a crime therein
enhancements: Burglary of a dwelling (§ 97-17-23, up to 25 years)
notes: Burglary of a dwelling carries up to 25 years. Burglary of other structures carries up to 7 years.

elements: Defendant broke and entered a dwelling house
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Burglary of a dwelling carries a mandatory minimum of 3 years. One of the most seriously punished property crimes in Mississippi.

elements: Defendant took and carried away a motor vehicle belonging to another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Motor vehicle theft is charged as grand larceny. Value determines the sentencing range.

elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of stolen property
Knowing or having reasonable grounds to believe it was stolen
notes: Same value thresholds as larceny. Knowledge of stolen character is an essential element.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously destroyed, damaged, or defaced property of another
notes: Mississippi uses 'malicious mischief' as the statutory term. Includes graffiti and vandalism.

elements: Defendant entered upon land of another
After being forbidden to do so by the owner or signs
Without permission
notes: Trespass after notice carries up to 6 months. Trespass on private property is common in rural Mississippi.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously damaged, destroyed, or defaced the property of another
notes: Covers property damage, tampering, and destruction. Restitution typically ordered.

elements: Defendant attempted to cause or purposely, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury
Against a current or former spouse, cohabitant, parent of a common child, or other family/household member
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (felony, up to 5 years or 10 years under § 97-3-7(4))
notes: Third DV offense is a felony regardless of severity. Aggravated domestic violence (§ 97-3-7(4)) carries up to 20 years.

elements: Defendant committed a battery against a domestic partner
Battery includes unwanted physical contact
notes: Mississippi uses the same statute for DV assault and battery. No separate battery statute.

elements: Defendant was a parent, guardian, or custodian of a child
Defendant willfully committed an act or omission
That caused or contributed to the neglect, abuse, or endangerment of the child
enhancements: Serious bodily harm results (up to 20 years)
Death of the child (life or 20–40 years)
notes: Mississippi has aggressive child protection enforcement. Death of a child from abuse carries 20–40 years or life.

penalty_max: 20 years (serious bodily harm); 40 years to life (death results)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused serious bodily injury to a child under 18
Defendant was a parent, guardian, custodian, or person having custody
enhancements: Death of the child (20–40 years or life)
notes: Death resulting from child abuse carries the harshest penalties. Mandatory reporting by professionals.

statute_title: Violation of Domestic Abuse Protection Order
elements: A valid protection order was in effect
Defendant had notice of the order
Defendant intentionally violated a condition of the order
notes: First violation is a misdemeanor. Second or subsequent, or violation with assault, is a felony.

elements: Defendant purposefully engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or the safety of others
Defendant knew or should have known the conduct would cause fear
enhancements: Violation of protective order while stalking
notes: Includes cyberstalking. Second or subsequent offense is a felony.

elements: Defendant engaged in conduct directed at a specific person
With intent to harass or annoy
Including following, telephoning repeatedly, or sending unwanted communications
notes: Harassment is a lesser offense than stalking. Includes telephone and electronic harassment.

statute_title: Exploitation or Abuse of Vulnerable Person
elements: Defendant willfully abused, neglected, or exploited a vulnerable person
Vulnerable person includes elderly or disabled adults
notes: Mississippi's vulnerable adult protection statute. Financial exploitation is aggressively prosecuted.

offense_class: Felony (prohibited persons); Misdemeanor (others in restricted areas)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
Defendant was a prohibited person (felon, minor, or intoxicated)
Or carried in a prohibited location
notes: Mississippi is a constitutional carry state (permitless open and concealed carry for most adults 18+). Restrictions remain for felons, certain locations, and persons under 18.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony
enhancements: Possession during commission of another felony
notes: Mandatory minimum of 1 year that cannot be suspended. Rights restoration available after certain waiting periods.

statute_title: Concealed Weapon — Prohibited Location or Person
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
In a prohibited location (courthouse, police station, school, etc.)
Or defendant was a prohibited person
notes: Mississippi adopted constitutional carry. Most adults 18+ can carry without a permit. Prohibited locations remain restricted.

statute_title: Discharge of Firearm in Prohibited Area
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
Within city limits or in a prohibited area
notes: Municipal ordinances may impose additional restrictions. Reckless discharge causing injury charged under separate statutes.

elements: Defendant knowingly used the personal identifying information of another
Without the other person's consent
With intent to obtain a benefit, credit, or goods
notes: Includes use of SSN, credit card numbers, and other personal data. Restitution ordered.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property, money, or goods by an employer or principal
Defendant fraudulently converted the property to personal use
notes: Mississippi has specific embezzlement statutes for public officials and employees.

elements: Defendant falsely made, altered, or counterfeited a written instrument
With intent to defraud
notes: Includes forging checks, deeds, and other legal instruments.

elements: Defendant counterfeited or forged currency, bank notes, or government obligations
notes: Federal counterfeiting charges typically apply. State charges may be concurrent.

elements: Defendant issued a check or draft
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Low threshold ($100) for felony bad check in Mississippi.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented a false or fraudulent insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Mississippi Department of Insurance investigates. Restitution typically ordered.

elements: Defendant used a credit card or credit card number
Knowing it was stolen, forged, or without authorization
To obtain goods, services, or money
notes: Low felony threshold ($250). Includes possession of stolen credit cards.

elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved was derived from criminal activity
With intent to promote criminal activity or conceal the source
notes: Federal money laundering charges may also apply.

elements: Defendant obtained property or money by false pretenses
With intent to cheat and defraud
notes: General fraud statute. Classification depends on value obtained.

penalty_max: 30 years (general); Life (victim under 14 or with weapon)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with another person
Without the victim's consent
By use of force, threat, or where victim was incapable of consent
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (up to life)
notes: Mississippi uses 'sexual battery' rather than 'rape' or 'sexual assault' in statutes. Separate statutory rape provisions under § 97-3-65.

elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with another person
By force, against the person's will, or with a person incapable of consent
Or with a person under 14 years of age
notes: Forcible rape can carry a death sentence in Mississippi for offenses involving minors under certain circumstances (though constitutionality is limited by Kennedy v. Louisiana).

elements: Defendant willfully and lewdly exposed their person or private parts
In a public place or in the presence of another
notes: Second offense or exposure to a minor is a felony. Sex offender registration may be required.

elements: Defendant offered or agreed to engage in sexual conduct
In exchange for compensation
notes: Low-level misdemeanor. Solicitation involving a minor carries enhanced felony penalties.

elements: Defendant used, employed, persuaded, or coerced a child under 18
To engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions
notes: Mississippi aggressively prosecutes child exploitation. Federal charges typically apply as well.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration
notes: Mississippi Sex Offender Registry. Registration may be required for life depending on the offense.

penalty_max: 30 years (victim 14-16 and defendant 3+ years older); Life (victim under 14)
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with a person under 16
Defendant was at least 36 months older than the victim
notes: Age of consent in Mississippi is 16. Close-in-age exception: within 36 months of age. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Defendant willfully disturbed the peace of another
By loud or offensive conduct
Or by threatening, quarrelsome, or otherwise disorderly behavior
notes: Low-level public order offense. Often charged alongside other offenses.

elements: A law enforcement officer attempted to make a lawful arrest
Defendant willfully opposed or resisted the officer
By use of force, threat, or intimidation
notes: Passive resistance generally is not sufficient. Must involve force, threat, or intimidation.

elements: Defendant obstructed, resisted, or opposed any officer or court
In the discharge of their official duties
notes: Broad obstruction statute. Covers interference with law enforcement, court proceedings, and government operations.

penalty_max: Varies; typically up to 6 months or until compliance
elements: A valid court order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully disobeyed the order
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive. Civil contempt is coercive — defendant can purge by compliance.

elements: Defendant was found drunk or intoxicated in a public place
And was disturbing others or endangering themselves
notes: Low-level offense. Many jurisdictions use protective custody rather than arrest.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (if underlying was misdemeanor); Felony (if underlying was felony)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant willfully failed to appear
notes: Bail jumping is charged based on the severity of the underlying offense.

elements: Defendant knowingly made a false report of a crime to law enforcement
Knowing the report was false
notes: Includes filing false police reports and making false emergency calls.

elements: Defendant willfully threatened to commit an act of violence
Against another person or their property
Putting the victim in reasonable fear
notes: Covers both verbal and written threats. Bomb threats and mass violence threats carry additional penalties.

elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath
In a judicial proceeding
Knowing the statement was false
Statement was material
notes: Includes testimony, depositions, and sworn affidavits.

elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public official
With intent to influence the official's action
notes: Covers both offering and receiving bribes. Mississippi has aggressive public corruption enforcement.

elements: Defendant was lawfully confined or in custody
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape
notes: Includes escape from prison, jail, and lawful custody during transport.

elements: Defendant intentionally or with criminal negligence tortured, mutilated, or cruelly killed a domesticated dog or cat
notes: Aggravated cruelty to dogs and cats is a felony. Simple animal cruelty (§ 97-41-1) is a misdemeanor.

penalty_max: Up to the maximum of the original sentence
elements: Defendant was on probation for a criminal conviction
Defendant violated a condition of probation
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose any sentence available at time of original conviction. Mississippi uses graduated sanctions.

elements: Defendant was on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Mississippi Parole Board conducts revocation hearings. Violator may serve remainder of original sentence.

elements: Defendant aided, counseled, or encouraged another person in the commission of a crime
notes: An accessory before the fact is punished the same as the principal in Mississippi.

offense_class: Generally one-half the maximum of the completed offense
penalty_max: Up to one-half the penalty of the completed offense
fine_max: Up to one-half the fine of the completed offense
elements: Defendant designed and endeavored to commit a crime
Defendant took a substantial step toward its commission
But failed to complete the offense
notes: Attempt is punished at up to half the penalty of the completed offense under Mississippi law.

offense_class: Felony (if target offense is felony); Misdemeanor (if target is misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a crime
An overt act was performed in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy to commit a felony is itself a felony. An overt act by any conspirator is required.

penalty_max: 30 years (labor trafficking); Life (sex trafficking of minor)
elements: Defendant knowingly recruited, enticed, harbored, transported, or obtained another person
Through force, fraud, or coercion
For the purpose of involuntary servitude, forced labor, or commercial sexual activity
enhancements: Victim is a minor (up to life)
notes: Mississippi enacted comprehensive anti-trafficking legislation. Safe harbor provisions for minor victims.

elements: Defendant restrained or confined another person
Without consent and without lawful authority
notes: Lesser included offense of kidnapping. Covers unlawful restraint without the specific intent elements of kidnapping.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed an opioid drug
Including heroin, fentanyl, or prescription opioids without valid prescription
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or church
notes: Opioid crisis has increased enforcement and prosecution in Mississippi. Fentanyl-related offenses are a priority.
